text:
Text-based recommendation gains alone do not establish semantic recurrence; TASTE explicitly links text matching to reduced popularity bias ([paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.14029)). Proposed retrained controls: ID-only SASRec; SASRec plus training-frequency features; metadata-presence/length-only features; fixed random item vectors; and item-text permutation within category × training-popularity × metadata-coverage strata. Preserve missingness and text-length distributions. Compare original text against boilerplate-stripped text and boilerplate-only text, deriving brand-like strings solely from available titles/descriptions. These controls test whether gains require correctly aligned descriptive content rather than popularity, coverage, item identity, or repeated commercial wording.

To isolate recurrence, retrain otherwise matched variants using mean pooling, recency-weighted pooling, last-item text, and the proposed recurrence mechanism. Add history-text order shuffling and suppression of repeated semantic matches while retaining the item-ID history; distinguish order sensitivity from repeated-content effects. Match training budgets, dimensions, and tuning opportunities; report paired differences and popularity/coverage strata. Keep all four categories and identical pinned candidates. Sampled-candidate findings should remain explicitly scoped to that task: candidate sampling interacts with popularity and need not preserve full-catalog conclusions ([study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.11723)).

Report every validation-informed trial, checkpoint-selection rule, search budget, and selected configuration; label best validation HR@10 as selection-affected. For paired bootstrap intervals, resample users within each category, retain model pairing, and recompute the equal-weight four-category macro difference. State that intervals condition on selected fitted models, seed 42, observed categories, and fixed candidates; they exclude training/search variability and do not correct selection optimism. Repeated selection can overfit validation ([Cawley–Talbot](https://www.jmlr.org/papers/volume11/cawley10a/cawley10a.pdf)). Freeze the final choice before host-held-out evaluation; broader uncertainty requires independently repeated training and selection, beyond these conditional intervals.
